forecasts.question: Will Nvidia report Q3 FY2027 total revenue of at least US$112.0bn?
forecasts.resolution: Resolves YES if GAAP total revenue for the fiscal quarter ending late October 2026, as stated in Nvidia's Q3 FY2027 earnings press release / 8-K (investor.nvidia.com, scheduled 18 Nov 2026), is >= US$112,000m. NO otherwise. If not reported by resolve_by, resolves NO.
indicators: Nvidia Q3 FY27 guidance: US$108.0bn +/-2% (26 Aug 2026)
Q2 FY27 revenue US$96.2bn vs US$91.0bn guide (+5.7%)
Hyperscaler 2026 capex plans (~US$600-800bn)
OpenAI revenue doubts / AI-stock selloff (Oracle -5.5% on 8 Oct)
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: Nvidia has beaten the midpoint of its revenue guide every quarter of the AI cycle, typically by ~3-6%; US$112bn needs a 3.7% beat on the US$108bn guide, which roughly two-thirds of recent quarters cleared (Q2 FY27 beat by 5.7%). Update this week: the 8 Oct FT report that OpenAI's run-rate revenue is ~US$50bn not ~US$70bn hit AI stocks, but that is a demand-durability worry for 2027, not a constraint on a quarter already nearly shipped; supply (CoWoS/HBM) rather than demand still caps upside. Net ~60%. (Manifold play-money market has ~53% on >=US$112bn; not a real-money crowd, so crowd_p left null.)

forecasts.question: Will the Fed raise the federal funds target range at its 8-9 December 2026 FOMC meeting?
forecasts.resolution: Resolves YES if the FOMC statement released at the conclusion of the 8-9 Dec 2026 meeting (federalreserve.gov) raises the upper bound of the federal funds target range above its level immediately before that meeting (any size). NO if held or cut.
indicators: Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026 (first hike since 2023)
Sep SEP: 16 of 18 officials see >=1 more hike in 2026
US 10y Treasury yield 5.36%, highest since 2002
Weak September payrolls cut hike odds
US CPI 3.4% y/y (Aug); Sep CPI due 14 Oct
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: when the Fed restarts hiking and the dot plot signals more, the signalled follow-up hike is delivered in roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of cases within the next two meetings. Update this week: the 10y at 5.36% and a 4%+ STI/global equity drawdown are tightening financial conditions on their own, which gives doves cover to pause, and the September jobs miss already pulled October odds to ~17%. Against that, CPI at 3.4% and the dots still point to one more move, with December the natural meeting. I shade below the crowd: 65% vs Kalshi ~77% (74% for +25bp plus 3% for >25bp, 13 Oct).

forecasts.question: Will the Category B COE premium close below S$120,000 in any open bidding exercise held from 14 Oct 2026 to 31 Jan 2027?
forecasts.resolution: Resolves YES if any LTA COE open bidding exercise result published between 14 Oct 2026 and 31 Jan 2027 shows a Category B Quota Premium below S$120,000 (source: LTA OneMotoring COE results / data.gov.sg). NO otherwise.
indicators: Cat B S$130,100 on 7 Oct 2026 (-2.2%), third straight fall from S$135,001 peak
Cat B has not closed below S$121,000 since March 2026
Nov 2026-Jan 2027 quota announcement due late Oct 2026
MAS tightening + Fed hikes + bank-stock selloff (wealth effect)
Cat B bids/quota ratio 1.19 on 7 Oct
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: Cat B needs a ~7.8% fall within about six exercises. Since April 2026 it has stayed in a S$121k-135k band, and drops of that size over three months happened only once in 2026 (Jan->Feb, -14% to S$105k, a seasonal/quota-driven dip). Update this week: three consecutive declines from the S$135k peak, thin bid cover (1.19x), a 4.1% weekly STI fall led by banks, and global rate rises all point to softening demand, which is Gate 3 of the S$80k thesis moving the right way. But the 2.2% step is small, and the quota for Nov-Jan is unknown; a flat-to-lower quota would keep premiums sticky. ~20%.

forecasts.question: Will the Straits Times Index close below 5,000 on any trading day before 31 March 2027?
forecasts.resolution: Resolves YES if the official FTSE Straits Times Index daily closing level is below 5,000.00 on any SGX trading day from 14 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 inclusive (source: SGX / FTSE Russell / Investing.com historical data). NO otherwise.
indicators: STI ~5,430 on 13 Oct 2026, ~7% below Sep all-time high of 5,828
STI -4.1% week to 9 Oct; DBS -5.0%, OCBC -8.4%, UOB -7.3%
US 10y at 5.36%
Bank Q3 results early Nov; MAS decision 14 Oct
DBS at 16.9x forward P/E vs 13.2x MSCI financials
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: 5,000 is ~8% below the current level. With STI realised vol of ~12-15% a year, a driftless index touches a level ~8% lower within 5.5 months roughly 30-40% of the time, and historically the STI goes years without such a drawdown in calm regimes. Update this week: the regime is not calm. The STI is already ~7% off its peak in a bank-led selloff driven by the highest US yields since 2002, and banks are ~40% of the index and trade at a premium multiple. Offsets: strong dividend support, and a 25% gain over the year means profit-taking rather than a fundamentals break so far. ~33%. Relevant to the watchlist: a YES would bring the banks much closer to (but still above) the April entry bands.

forecasts.question: Will the WTI crude oil spot price close at or above US$115 per barrel on any day before 31 December 2026?
forecasts.resolution: Resolves YES if the EIA daily Cushing, OK WTI spot price (series RWTC, eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/rwtcD.htm) is >= US$115.00 for any trading day from 14 Oct 2026 to 31 Dec 2026 inclusive. NO otherwise.
indicators: WTI ~US$93.3, Brent ~US$106 on 13 Oct 2026 (Brent highest close since 15 Sep)
Tanker attacks near Hormuz; Houthi strike on Riyadh airport
OPEC cut 2026 demand-growth forecast to 0.4 mb/d from 1.4 mb/d
US temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel / diesel supply
US 10y at 5.36% and Fed hiking: demand headwind
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: WTI needs a ~23% rise in about 11 weeks. At the ~40-45% annualised volatility of this war-risk regime, a driftless price touches a level ~1 sigma above spot about 30% of the time intraday, and somewhat less on daily closes. Update this week: supply risk flared again (Hormuz tanker attacks, Houthi strike on Riyadh), lifting Brent to its highest close in a month. Demand-side signals point the other way: OPEC slashed its demand-growth forecast, Washington is easing Russian fuel supply, and rising global rates weigh on activity. Spikes in this regime have faded rather than compounded. ~20%, below Kalshi's ~30%, which also counts intraday highs and so sits slightly above a daily-close rule. Feeds Gate 1 (oil physical spot) of the Cat B thesis.

forecasts.question: Will the FAO Food Price Index for December 2026 be above 136.0 points?
forecasts.resolution: YES if the FAO Food Price Index value for December 2026, as first published by FAO (fao.org/worldfoodsituation/foodpricesindex, ~early Jan 2027), is > 136.0. NO otherwise. Later revisions are ignored.
indicators: FFPI 136.0 in Sep 2026 (highest since Nov 2022)
Sugar +6.1% m/m, cereals +5.1% m/m (US corn, Black Sea)
Brent >US$100: fertiliser, freight, biofuel demand for veg oils
Northern Hemisphere harvest pressure; meat index easing
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: monthly FFPI moves are usually within +/-2% and a 3-month change is close to a coin flip, with mild momentum. Update: September rose to 136.0, the highest since November 2022, led by sugar (third straight rise) and cereals on weaker US corn yields and Black Sea disruption; oil above US$100 keeps input and freight costs high. Offsetting: seasonal harvest pressure and falling meat prices. Slight lean to YES on momentum and energy pass-through. Feeds the pricing-power read on Nestle/P&G/Unilever and Wilmar margins.

forecasts.question: Will SP Group's Q1 2027 household electricity tariff (before GST) be higher than Q4 2026's 28.59 cents/kWh?
forecasts.resolution: YES if the low-tension household tariff for 1 Jan-31 Mar 2027, before GST, announced by SP Group (spgroup.com.sg tariff information / media release, ~end Dec 2026), is > 28.59 cents/kWh. NO if equal or lower.
indicators: Brent ~US$103-106 in mid-Oct vs lower Jul-Aug levels
Oil-indexed LNG/piped gas costs for SG gencos
Rystad expects single-digit Q1 2027 increase
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: SP Group sets the tariff off fuel costs in the first ~2.5 months of the prior quarter, so the direction of the quarterly change follows oil-linked gas costs between windows in the large majority of quarters. Update: Q4 fell 10.4% because July-August oil was much lower; Brent rallied from mid-September and is ~US$103-106 in October on Gulf/Hormuz shipping risk, and Rystad expects a single-digit rise for Q1 2027. Main risks are a sharp oil reversal before early December or a downward network-cost revision. Electricity tariffs are one of the eight COE-thesis gates.

forecasts.question: Will the front-month JKM LNG futures contract settle above US$20.00/MMBtu on 31 December 2026?
forecasts.resolution: YES if the CME 'LNG Japan/Korea Marker (Platts) Futures' nearest listed contract month (expected Feb 2027) has a daily settlement > US$20.00/MMBtu on 31 Dec 2026 (or the last CME settlement day of 2026), per CME Group settlements. NO otherwise.
indicators: JKM high-US$24s/MMBtu on 2 Oct (pre-Hormuz-closure ~US$10.6)
US-Iran ceasefire talks / Hormuz shipping status
Qatar LNG force majeure (since Mar 2026)
EU storage 72% on 2 Oct, 17.5% below 5-yr avg; NE Asia winter weather
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: front-month JKM rarely moves more than ~20% over a 2.5-month window outside of supply shocks, which on its own favours staying above US$20 from the mid-24s. Update: prices are being held up by the Hormuz closure and Qatar's force majeure, with Europe's low storage competing for cargoes into winter; but weak Chinese/Korean buying, a mild-winter outlook and progress in US-Iran ceasefire talks already knocked JKM ~US$1-2 lower last week, and a reopening would collapse the risk premium quickly. That binary makes this a genuine coin flip. Feeds SG's gas-fired power costs with a lag.

forecasts.question: Will Singapore's food inflation for December 2026 be 2.5% year-on-year or higher?
forecasts.resolution: YES if the food inflation rate (y/y) for December 2026 in the MAS-MTI 'Consumer Price Developments in December 2026' release (~late Jan 2027) is >= 2.5%. NO if lower.
indicators: SG food inflation 2.1% Jun, 2.2% Jul, 2.3% Aug 2026
FAO Food Price Index 136.0 in Sep (highest since Nov 2022)
Energy/freight pass-through (Brent >US$100)
MAS S$NEER slope (stronger SGD damps imported food costs)
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: SG food inflation moves slowly, typically 0.1-0.2pp a month, so a 0.2pp rise over four months is roughly even odds when the trend is up. Update: food inflation has edged up three months running to 2.3% in August, global food commodities hit a near-four-year high in September, and high energy and freight costs are feeding food services; offsetting, MAS has tightened three times this year and a stronger SGD cushions imported-food costs, and hawker/food-services prices are sticky but rarely accelerate fast. Slightly below even.

forecasts.question: Will Walmart U.S. report Q3 FY2027 comparable sales growth (ex-fuel) of 3.0% or more?
forecasts.resolution: YES if Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth excluding fuel for the quarter ending ~31 Oct 2026, as reported in Walmart's Q3 FY2027 earnings release (stock.walmart.com / 8-K, ~mid-late Nov 2026), is >= 3.0%. NO if lower.
indicators: Walmart U.S. comps +2.6% in Q2 FY27 (slowest in ~6 years), ~80bp health & wellness drag
FY27 net sales guide raised to 4-5%; Q3 sales guide +3.0-3.75% cc
US consumer under higher rates (Fed hiking, 10y 5.3%) and fuel >US$90 WTI
Trade-down from higher-income shoppers
forecasts.rationale: Base rate: Walmart U.S. comps ran ~4-5% for most of FY24-FY26, so 3% used to be a low bar, but the latest print was 2.6% and comps rarely re-accelerate by 40bp+ in one quarter without a calendar or pricing tailwind. Update: management raised full-year sales guidance, transactions are growing and trade-down tends to help Walmart in a squeeze; against that, the health-and-wellness drag persists, the Fed is hiking and fuel is expensive, which hurts lower-income discretionary baskets. Lean NO. A read on staples volumes vs pricing power.
